# Cloud replay test vectors

These files are vendored test vectors for the Titanwarden Cloud protocol. Each
directory name under this folder is a fixed vector set ID that the tests refer
to by path. The SHA256 tables below are the reference for these files. The
tests hash a vector and compare it with its expected SHA256 before parsing, so
a changed byte fails the test instead of changing what it checks.

The PR 1 and PR 3 files below are in vector set
`177766e1de71acbff0a188fa4d4b487db6c28391`.
The original B1-B3 bytes and hashes are unchanged from vector set 6a2d52f. SHA256 is checked before JSON
decoding. K1 is kept as its original TypeScript source and hashed before
inspection. No fixture is regenerated by the Python tests.

B1 consumes all 356 V0 cases, all V1 founder cases, all V2 sections and V3
indices 6 and 8 through 12. V3 case identity includes file, array index and
value type; duplicate display names remain distinct.

The ten production v2 traces contain 106 accepted records and 159 negative
cases. PR 1 independently verifies all 99 B1-B3 records from genesis, covering
every authority, epoch and ciphertext kind, and all 142 non-binding negative
cases. All provided predecessor and resulting core states, canonical bytes,
hashes, policy signatures, epoch hashes, snapshots, commitments and custody
are compared. Five trailing B6 suffix entry points fail closed with
`E_POLICY_CONFLICT`; no checkpoint or permissive fixture verifier is used.

The authority_core projection includes retired recovery points and excludes
recovery_protocol metadata, as defined by the paired cloud fixture contract.
Full authority hashes and final states remain in the fixtures and their byte
integrity is checked. Complete replay of all ten traces and all 159 negatives,
including B6 typed bindings and final slot availability, is a broker PR 3 gate.

PR 3 additionally consumes every indexed V3 case and all 19 V5 cases. Its
opt-in recovery verifier replays all 106 production records and all 159
negatives from genesis, including every trailing typed-binding suffix. It
compares the full authority hash and state, recovery metadata, epoch state,
commitments and custody, and verifies final retained slot availability. The
original B1-B3 verifier and its refusal boundary remain independently tested.

Reference-only v1 traces establish schema, digest and signature bytes only.
They are explicitly refused as production acceptance evidence. The v1 typed
binding trace supplies a verified B1-B3 prefix, then remains outside PR 1.

An earlier vector set lacked the complete signed authority and epoch bundles
required by the plan. The current set adds them; it changes fixture evidence
only, with no cloud protocol or runtime configuration changes. Positive
adoption-root and first real founding broker certificate traces remain absent
from these bundles, so those paths retain
mandatory independently verified provenance ports and no enrollment caller.

## Broker PR 2 primitive additions

The following file is in vector set
`6a2d52f7cfcd9be944cb880602007832de637dc0`:

| Path | SHA256 |
| --- | --- |
| control/src/enroll/vectors/enrollment-v1.json | d664576d9f2776e8389d38439bc9c72ed65e758a8201d8eb15f026651bb3fdaa |

PR 2 consumes every one of its twelve cases, including raw canonical request
contexts, duplicate-query rejection, noncanonical/duplicate-body rejection,
join/reservation/root proof separation and all three adoption keyring AADs.
These are primitive vectors, with admission assertions for the request cases;
they do not by themselves establish a complete production enrollment flow.
Legacy AAD is covered by V0's unchanged 356-case consumer. Local crash tests
exercise disposable copies and do not manufacture replacement cloud fixtures.


## Broker PR 2 production enrollment supplement

The following vectors are in vector set
`177766e1de71acbff0a188fa4d4b487db6c28391`. The unchanged V4 primitive bytes above
match the same set. The original PR 1 fixture bytes retain their SHA256 without regeneration;
PR 3 keeps them in the same set.

| core/vectors/broker-enrollment-adopt-v3.json | 08c6b365b8c3ca7da013cebbcba742b898b1a002a82a8d8b955ff4f0bdeac77f |
| core/vectors/broker-request-admission-v3.json | 74bb98112c9895d3343680b6b3ec2bb0c2136f02eb72ceb44ee0e87f7ca8c34a |
| core/vectors/paired-broker-manifest-enrollment-v1.json | 2ff2581fc1ff717439327688475dad7c35cc0c9065bd11dff66b50c88b2081f8 |

Three traces contain 39 steps and 13 recorded refusals on the full production
profile. The consumer checks all hashes and step counts, every response and
refusal rollback snapshot, 17 signed broker transports with exact forwarding
bytes, all four clock boundaries, nonce replay, same-UUID fresh-nonce reads,
query canonicalization, empty POST/body rejection and lost-response retry
convergence. It replays the join from genesis through the real signed broker
certificate with concrete evidence, compares the independently derived state,
checks local SAS bytes/words and opens the committed OMK into local BLK custody.
It also replays the signed adoption genesis and epoch from zero, verifies both
proofs, and confirms legacy ingestion and first-certificate prerequisites stay
closed. It neither imports a seeded authority state nor manufactures cloud
results. Supplemental private JWKs and OMK bytes are public deterministic test
material generated for these vectors and explicitly marked as such, never user credentials.

The join supplement covers full-broker initial custody. A positive scoped
initial unseal trace is not supplied; scoped commitment semantics are covered
by PR 1 production replay, and PR 2 retains that explicit coverage limit. The
first real founding broker certificate cannot be approved on the production
adoption profile without the still-disabled first human owner claim. Its
recorded refusal is the acceptance boundary, not a reason to synthesize a
certificate or skip authority verification.

The companion consumers independently replay all 150 accepted entries and 76
negative policy cases, starting at pinned genesis with each case's exact
operational prefix. They compare full authority and epoch state/hash, heads,
snapshots, commitments and custody, request and grant projections, pending reset
records and immutable proposal/activation receipts. All 20 operational cases
verify their canonical request/response bytes and preserve policy authority;
private slot and wrap bytes are checked against signed commitments. Server-side
notice and quota metadata is pinned evidence, not a broker endpoint implementation.
Historical reset replay additionally uses retained acceptance despite a later
cancelled operational row and never calls a live SAS gate.

Positive nonholder-to-owner recovery remains refused by the existing genesis
wrapper, and broker-founded recovery_set remains unreachable before a first
human owner can be certified. Both boundaries are explicit rejection fixtures.
No remote checkpoint is accepted as authority and no production caller is enabled.

The original K1 TypeScript fixture and broker genesis v2 fixture also remain
in vector set 6a2d52f, with identical bytes, so existing literal
consumers from PRs 1 and 2 keep their original paths.
